name: 7-Card Brag
description: 7-Card Brag is a strategic partition variant of the British vying game Brag. Every player is dealt seven cards and must divide them into two independent three-card hands, leaving one card as a 'discard' (muck). This variant offers the highest level of hand optimization in the partition family, allowing players to build extremely strong combinations from their seven cards. Once partitions are set, play follows the traditional British vying structure where bluffing and 'Blind' betting are key.

history.origins: Developed as a high-skill extension of standard 3-Card Brag, 7-Card Brag appeared in card rooms as a faster-playing alternative to 9-Card Brag (Crash). It emphasizes the tactical discard of the seventh card to perfectly balance two hands.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Multi-hand Brag variants evolve in the UK.
1980s: 7-Card variant becomes a staple of high-stakes social gaming.
Present: Popular in British card clubs and as a digital competitive format.
history.cultural: Regarded as a game of 'perfect balance', where the ability to split 7 cards into two winning three-card units is the hallmark of a master player.
history.evolution: The addition of a seventh card and a muck mechanic allows for much more flexible hand construction than the rigid 6-card or 9-card partition variants.

setup.dealing: Deal seven cards face-down to each player. Players divide their cards into two three-card hands and muck the seventh card.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, betting chips or currency.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest-ranked hands across the partition or by forcing others to fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Partition**: Players split 7 cards into Hand A (3 cards), Hand B (3 cards), and 1 Muck card. 2. **Vying**: Standard Brag betting follows. Players choose to play 'Blind' (before seeing the 7 cards) or 'See'. 3. **Ranks**: Prial > Running Flush > Run > Flush > Pair > High Card.
keyRules: Both three-card hands must be legal Brag combinations.
In many house rules, a player must win both comparisons to sweep the pot.
A Seeing player bets double the cost of a Blind player.

strategy.basic: Use the seventh card to remove a rank that doesn't fit into a pair or sequence. With 7 cards, you should aim for at least two Flushes or one strong Run.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Sacrifice' Discard: If you have a choice between making one almost-unbeatable Prial or two very strong Runs, the two Runs are often statistically safer for winning multi-hand comparisons.
strategy.advanced: Kicker Optimization: When building your two hands, ensure Hand B (the weaker hand) has the highest possible kickers. Many rounds are won on Hand B tie-breakers.
tips: Track the mucked cards in your head—knowing which ranks are 'dead' helps you read opponent partitions.
Don't ignore the Blind bet; the half-price advantage is massive even with 7 cards to choose from.

variations.name: 6-Card Brag
variations.description: Partitioning six cards with no muck card.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Engine-level overrides for 6-Card Brag are not yet modeled; this entry only links the closely related partition variant.

scoring.description: Standard pot-based resolution across dual-hand comparisons.
scoring.winCondition: Win both hand comparisons OR be the last player standing.

synthesis.shortDescription: The ultimate test of hand management in the Brag family. Partition seven cards into two separate units and choose the perfect muck card to maximize your win-probability. With more information and better combinations, 7-Card Brag is the preferred choice for strategic vying.
